transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep making careless mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and on reports I’ll copy the wrong numbers from the dashboard, or I’ll miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. Even when I think I’ve gone over it, something still gets missed, and it’s starting to be a real problem.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even about everyday things?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I worry about work when something goes wrong, but I don’t know if I’d say I worry a lot about everyday things. It’s not something I’ve really noticed as the main issue.
Looking back, did you have similar problems with attention or careless mistakes when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. My mom still brings it up sometimes—like notes from my elementary school teachers saying I rushed through assignments, lost homework, talked out of turn, and had trouble staying in my seat unless someone reminded me. So it’s not exactly new.
Do these attention problems also cause trouble for you outside of work?

Yeah, it does. Work is the biggest place it shows up—my manager actually put it in a formal review because of the mistakes and missed follow-through.

But it affects home too. People get frustrated with me because they feel like they can’t count on me to do what I said I’d do, and that turns into arguments sometimes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent pattern of inattentive and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood, with clinically significant impairment at work and at home. Confirmed symptoms include repeated careless mistakes, missed procedural details, losing homework in childhood, talking out of turn, and difficulty remaining seated. This supports ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation / disturbance of activity and attention, and there was no stronger evidence for an anxiety-based primary disorder.
